The Fabric Fund paid £12,600 on 2024-06-17 to patch the crack. Its condition is that if the hearth comes out of the forge before 2034-06-17 while you hold the premises, you must repay £12,600 in full within 28 days. The Estate's plan breaks the hearth out by 2026-10-31 — you hold the premises, and that is eight years before the trigger date. The repayment obligation fires. With the work done during the October shutdown (2026-10-19 to 2026-10-31), the 28-day clock starts running inside October, so repayment will fall due in November 2026. Set against the £18,000 the Estate is paying you, your net position is £5,400.

Everything else is largely unchanged. The new hearth is the same size and carries the same two fires, so you lose no capacity. The work lands inside your planned shutdown, so no trading days are lost. Your tools, anvils and order book are yours and unaffected. Halvard Quillon-Rees remains booked through 2027-12-31.

On the Workshop Continuity Grant: your lease runs from 2023-05-02 unbroken, and the 2027 round opens 2027-01-11. Three years back from that date is 2024-01-11, well after your lease started. Holding the premises while the Estate works on the building during your shutdown is not a break in your tenure, so your eligibility for the January 2027 grant round is intact. The lease offer deadline (2026-12-19) is also untouched.
